title: Folk-Tales of Angola
author: Héli Chatelain (collector); informants named in the notes
rights: Public domain (published 1894; collector d. 1908). Scan and OCR: Internet Archive.
citation: Chatelain, Héli. Folk-Tales of Angola: Fifty Tales, with Ki-mbundu Text, Literal English Translation, Introduction, and Notes. Memoirs of the American Folk-Lore Society 1. Boston and New York: Houghton, Mifflin, 1894.
editorialMarkers: Fifty Mbundu tales dictated to Chatelain in Loanda and along the Kuanza, printed in Kimbundu with his literal English. The Kimbundu is the primary text; the English is deliberately literal. Chatelain’s notes name each tale’s informant.
method: Layout-aware OCR (DjVu XML word coordinates): tales open at a centred Roman numeral, first for the Kimbundu text and again for the English; paragraphs by indent and vertical gap, joined across pages when unterminated; Kimbundu and English paragraphs paired by order (tale I, printed interlinear, is split by the language of each line); endnotes “NO. n.” attach Chatelain’s informant note to the tale. Units with no English counterpart keep the Kimbundu as their text. OCR errors are not corrected.
